Listen to my voice: You can hear music on a radio or television set.

We have invented machines that help our voices go out over long distances. These same machines also pick up other sounds from far away. Perhaps there are noises made by animals as well as those of humans. Our ears cannot tell where these distant sounds come from; yet we know their source. Can we be sure that man was the only creature created with this ability?
The human brain is capable of receiving, processing, and acting upon information picked up through its sense organs. It may act consciously, or it may work without being aware of itself at all. The soul, however, does not operate according to any of our senses. Its operation is mysterious to us—just as the ways in which a computer performs calculations are mysterious to an ordinary person.

If we could imagine a place where everything was perfect, would you go there? Wouldn't it be boring if everything were the way you wanted it? There'd have to be some room for change, and for being surprised by new things. If all your friends and family were with you, and the weather was nice, and the food was good—wouldn't that seem like too much of an ideal world? Well, the thing is, in such a place as that, nobody else would be alive. All those people are dead, and their souls went somewhere else after they died. And you might find out someday that what you're thinking about isn't so bad after all.

I wish I had never been born! But then again...why did I ever come into existence? The sun shines on my face every day. It's bright enough to blind me, but I still can't help looking up at it. It was around three o'clock when she opened her eyes. She could feel herself lying down inside a box. Outside the walls were made from something hard like wood. She was scared stiff at first, and began to scream and cry for her mommy.

However, the only reply that came back was a loud bang—and a flash of light. Her body started shaking uncontrollably. For a moment, the terror overwhelmed everything else, and the girl lost all sense of self. Then, slowly, things seemed to return to normal—but not quite. What had happened felt like a dream. After that, however, the memory became clearer and clearer until she recalled it completely. "Where am I?" asked the girl.
"You are in your new home." The voice came from nowhere. The child looked all around, but couldn't find anyone or anything.
"Who said that? And where is this place?"

The four friends came from all over the world—Moscow, Osaka, Sydney, and Baltimore.
Some called them a rock band—they were talented and extremely popular, at least until the band started
performing songs that were their own, and not from the ska band The Aquabats.

The new songs were often satanic and sometimes used violent imagery to teach lessons in free speech and freedom of religion. As they kept on gaining in popularity and fanbase, however, things began to fall apart, and the band members went in opposite directions, each turning out solo projects. Some people liked this approach, because it wasn't over-hyped, but it left an odd sense of emptiness. Most people didn't seem to really care who had actually composed the song—only that the musicians were still famous enough that it was cool to like them.
The first to leave the band was one of their frontman's friends and also their youngest member—they'd been with the band the longest.
The band's name was: B.O.A.Z.

The O is capitalized for no real reason—because if you spelled it without the capital letter, it could have been a threat. B, is for Babylon. It's also a double meaning that fits right into what the band was doing and represented. A, stands for Anarch. The Z stands for...you guessed it...the zodiac! The B represents the best and the worst in humanity at the same time: It stands for The Blackness and The Brightness. This makes for the band's symbol, as well as the meaning behind the title they adopted in their solo acts. The A was a sort of reward for having read the lyrics in order.

A reward you wouldn't normally want because you would never need it again. A reward you'd probably get if you actually turned into a beast or monster and ripped the living souls from the living bodies of all your enemies and pets. B was what the beast inside all of us wanted: All our worldly belongings. This was how it began, this was how it stayed, and this was how it will be—our whole life is just B's and A's.

Then we broke some bottles over his head—not a beer, one of the expensive whiskey bottles he'd bought from the mini-mart with his dad's credit card. I liked to keep it quiet from the dorm counselors and everyone else that my family bought the building and was supposed to

live in it themselves. Dad was pretty happy—his two younger children with no plans of joining a band in his eyes, as long as we could stay in school.

Now that our time's run out, here are some more facts for ya—like how the new kid in our midst and his friends actually liked it when their stuff was tossed up around—a few things even ended up under their beds. How these five total strangers never saw a damn thing and were probably the biggest partiers of the four—me too. The other rules: A, everyone must feel in their minds they've changed places in some sort of reality that might actually happen when all we're just trying to forget the truth is that our worldly possessions are pretty lame compared to whatever a band could actually have and put behind itself—it would all change when our music had a home...and b, no one, and I mean no one, is going to say they didn't feel anything—let me give
Rule O

and that's Order the name of a little league band a long time ago when they all looked like babies to us in the club—the most important thing you should know: There was some confusion about the new guy, a mix-up: One day we found he wasn't just the new kid. He'd become a group of his own that no one knew about. Then later, they never turned up in any of our songs ever again, which was fine. For all of us in The Band we lived those songs until one day the war finally stopped: It wasn't too bad a place to be: a home in The Blackness that was just your own home...
oh yeah, Rule Z

was make it stop...so let us have it as the four of us held this new kid down in bed—a piece of furniture I guess the kid had bought from his own dad who didn't really know about it, that we found by mistake and had ripped apart all around to see. It wasn't easy holding the new guy down as he threw up in my lap but there I was trying not to stare as we ripped his books and clothes off of him—then we locked ourselves inside the bathroom. For us this would be one more battle to get him out of here, in my book a much better revenge for a day than shitting our guts out in the stalls as everyone walked by: the little one's curse is they love their life the way you could

. And it was that night I realized, my God is B.O.A.Z. the spirit that descends when we are gathered in B.O.A.Z.'s name! Blessed be!
That's why I have a 2000 page exigesis about what the letters in B.O.A.Z. stands for. In fact, it is 6 AM, while this kid is unconscious, I shall read to you all from the pages of me exigesis:

B, for...birth, of course...you could even think about an upside-down bottle as it rises over our heads and what it stands for when we become monsters. We're gonna find a way to live happily...in the midst of an upside-down world: a black sky to show the whole wide world, the sea below to let us feel at home...B...that is the great divide of human experience, between blackness and brightness: an impenetrable darkness or an inviolable light. In fact, think of a person. To be alive is to be surrounded by darkness—no light can ever penetrate us; all we can know of another soul is through its darkness and brightness.

It's impossible for a person to live without one of them ever entering the other's body; even death, when it comes to the end, won't completely turn one away. In order to reach heaven we have to break through all the darkness...that which stands between us. Even more to the point is this: if one doesn't go through the light...through that same great divide, he might live to be a hundred years old. Even for a devil or demon to keep one from rising up—and so B is also an all-inclusive world: birth and the light are two of the three stages of the human life, but it can never be said how we end up because when the light leaves and a person goes under...

I have chosen! I will begin at Asyut!

Fantastic! Let us ride, my love!
But the follies of my youth… I wish you hadn't spoken of that, but I don't feel much regret now, I am sure you can tell.
It was all I had hoped for and dreamed of—that someone should listen. That someone would hear. That someone would say that he knows what that means… I believe… that he can do something… It is time! It is long, long time… It is time to save the world from war and… From what has happened. The future is something, but it will come only to those who save themselves!… It will come!

And it will find us not dead in a hole under ruins!
Come!
There was no discussion; I went straight to the Trolley, to the right tram stop. On the platform waited an electric train which would carry us up the line toward the Sun and up into space. There we could settle everything… You know my ideas, dear… Of course. My dreams are wide open! A lot has changed, you see! But what a journey to undertake! Let's be off… Let's leave this train now!
Come!
All this world is one great big storehouse and everything that was ours belongs now to all. Everything must become public… Public property!

To whom was anything ever stolen, but to those who were so poor, they never knew what they owned. There should be no poor, you see—if that were the case then I would… But what are we thinking about? And whom are we speaking to? You, you must remember what I dreamed about as I walked along the corridor at midnight. My own happiness—how was it? Who made it mine? What have you been dreaming, dear, but… and this, now? Where were we before we dreamed of what has never existed in the world and won't—so my love—can! You and I are leaving—going away together now—away, to another world!
Game: Um, so what about Asyut?

I got some bonus, and my love and I left town… So where were we then, or am I too dumb to see? We have found what was stolen from us in the world—we've seen and been through what they've all kept hidden so that you might, when you look about and think and use your head and say what you really meant… See nothing… Do nothing! You think of your life and can only wonder… You try to recall yourself… Only now you don't have anyone to look for… There's no one for whom you might stand… No one in your whole wide world except me—I am so cold!… And we… we had no such luck—no chance of winning and living… we are getting away… There will

be a happy moment now—don't doubt this for a moment, because we will soon find the rest!… And if we should come to harm on this journey we will find a way—this way is easy—this way is to go with me wherever it may be and you'll see everything.… You see? No, don't see; forget it—as long as you don't remember we will always be as if we did see… Ah… Let it go.… Let the memory fade.
So I really will have a little vacation… a rest… and be done with everything… because it has all become useless. You understand! The whole world… everything.
Raging Rapper's Ally is displeased, and looking to cut a bitch. Namely, you the bitch.

You'll learn you are the only bitch he will let you cut, which is a grave mistake because the little dog bitch you just cut is going to come looking for your life… so you may not have much to come back for. This is now a land war of unprecedented destruction. Our air war may be unprecedented but now I see more artillery on both sides, with our side's sidekick. I'm sorry; this is very old fashioned for a warrior to say; the more of the other guy's shit we are shooting off at the same time as we shoot the hell out of each other… the less effect it has; or worse: the sidekick takes over our own weapons and starts shooting.

There's got to be something else—in this day of atomic energy and ultimate devastation. How to be subtle… There are non-radioactive shells, as they now call them. I mean they may not make me so sick at the end of a long day and into my heartache—you understand—when it goes "whum," whooo-oo-m… right down deep where my soft spots are; into my lungs where my trouble-spots live, whoo-oo-m, down my arteries, down my spine, whummm!—whoooo-ooo-mmmmmmm!
Here I am sitting by a lake in our very own Sun Valley and they won't even let me ride my T-Bone… because

I have been living for the past half year at the New Age. And for those of us in the counter-intelligence section… some things are considered a risk! Here in this situation… a dangerous risk is being taken! What we've known of Raging Rapper for a year now, of his men and their locations in every province of the known world, must have given some in the highest political places and secret security forces and in the ever-secret services more cause for alarm! What you call security and they call "state secret," I call security for you and security against you, you know? That's their kind of state secret and how to protect them they do!

You may get rid of a soldier or a bureaucrat, but if you get rid of their work? You may never know it because you won't have been a party to it—only some spy will find out that Raging Rapper has a brother who doesn't really have any "Brother." Of course we think all he has are a few hangers-on he collects in his underground camp in some state whose name isn't even on the map any longer. They want me to catch them that way: as an end and not a beginning… but then of course it isn't I who get to pick up their dimes… which I shall continue to do until and only when they wish I hadn't—in fact when it will hurt them—when it will

hurt them enough… but by then, of course, it may be too late! You will excuse me for repeating that—my own use of humor when the pain is just too bad… When their own pain has put me in agony over it… Do you ever wonder where and what you have come from, the human animal… the most noble, most dignified of them all. Where did it begin? How much has it grown from its original cell in a gelatinous mud? Have you ever known… all that pain you take from a beating—the one with the whip that strikes all the nerve and leaves not an inch of you without red blood on your white hide.

dataFragment.data:
Sackcloth and Ashes Representative: Would you like to transform your pain into being a vessel for the Lord of Your Choice's Message? If so, you can either petition for penance with the Raging Rapper, or you can cast your lot with a random deity.
She-Who-Bittes-The Crabs-In-Half: Hmm, I detect a randomness theme today. Okay, randomness it is. Lay a deity on me!

… Pick any random deity. And the message is for that deity or its client. But now get up. You have two minutes in which to move into a certain area, or something shall happen that shall… you shall see… an immediate thing shall happen—you must walk with your knees high because we must know whether you can take the sudden shocks and… I must have an estimate as to where you will go. But why am I telling you? You're there… in your… Yes… Yes… I think I knew. Well then! If we know where you will go and the manner in which it will come to pass, then we know when it is a random thing and we must choose to run this matter to its finish!

The two-minute bit has run its course, which is an unfortunate thing… for your new job, if we ever know where you are going to end up—the bad part, if I might be so bold as to point this out to you… but it's always wise for them to be informed… Do you realize what would be required in that two-minute stretch for one such as yourself to change a random thing for a completely sure thing, a godly thing? Well, maybe there is a god behind the thing of which you must speak—something of a trickster. Who is this person? Is he one of the three major gods, as described by the Persian legends?
Sackcloth and Ashes Repreentative: Ahhhhh,

you know… those stories about a thing that goes around—hides and jumps out on you, then out there jumps you on a barbed hook… Oh yes… there were three… they… all have different names but they were not sure which one was correct.
She-Who-Bittes-The Crabs-In-Half: Do I look like the one they call Azhi Dahaka—or Kour Dahaka—the Thousand Hands of the Wasp, whose eyes are each the same as yours; is she or he or it in league with Raging Rapper's older brother? What I would like to know is how he could manage to do what we now know he must have done;

after all, isn't this some special state-of-mind we speak of that leads a being to such deeds of mind? Ah, I know how it must have been: he took up some non-state secret as his personal task, because he wasn't going to stand still for his state secrets!… but the three eyes! You speak to all these gods, who were said to be three; was that one of them you spoke to—is it here and will it attack us! Ahh, he must be somewhere… Yes.… Yes. I have looked before, and he may not have been at the gathering and yet I… Yes! There. Now do you understand me!

? Here is a state-of-mind that exists; the man was just an image of something.
Sackcloth and Ashes Representative: You will stop me and I shall obey and follow. For if a thing that goes around you is more than your eyes can handle, if that thing is larger than any eyesight of a person in all of this world can tell, then do the eyes tell a false truth and then we will no longer believe in this whole human existence and let the beast take its own wild course to eat anything it may meet in this world; because the world itself will not protect you because of the random thing's control of the beast—which has existed for ever in your creation as well.

But here in our very midst… he, she… or it! If that thing were ever in control of its mind it is in the hands of this one you point out—as we all have hands of clay in our palms… Oh, is that true? Ah… but why speak about the man—do the fingers do the writing; who knows the number of hands it can get through; at what moment does he write out his handwritten will. How do you know that you know the other fingers—is it possible to count and prove a random hand—by accident and by touch, where even an unnumbered touch or by chance can send your finger writing on to where it… they… won't let go of us anymore.

So, oh, let us get through it in an unnumbered, random number; in a moment we shall lose it all! You must read what your fingers say that is in your writing. Do we… no!… does our fingers speak and our heart tells and say to our very hand how our writing shall look or feel. Do you… the fingers of your hand—I think… what am I thinking? We… have you been asking… thinking too fast; I do not remember now… maybe, it should be the fingers in our minds. I should think of those… we must have two minutes… We cannot be found here—if we don't run to find them first!

Do your fingers in your mind say any and every possible random thing: one minute in our two minutes you'll get through some number and come out of your mind with more than our two minutes have covered; it would be for good then, then you must save yourself—while the god-things see it coming and don't stop it or say you go this way—
Sackcloth and Ashes Representative: Omm-ing Amm! I have a terrible suspicion of these hands now! This thing I see may be the one called Zorath. Do I ask this of all gods… let all know? That I have to choose. That I shall take one.

If the gods be called then that thing, and he or it that stands next to him… No!
She-Who-Bittes-The Crabs-In-Half: Oh yes! Oh, then I suppose you didn't need my time out at all and that if you are a fast thinker then your thoughts shall never get off the ground, let alone a choice on one… shall they? So go ahead with it, she thinks you have just told me: who do I make as a choice to hold his place by you… only then do we run for two minutes to keep ahead… You must. You will find something that has to be told that will be… No!
(The role of She WHo Bites The Crabs In Half Has Changed. Name forthcoming.)

Sackcloth and Ashes Representative: She-who-bites-the-crabs-in-half shall see how I'm done to get on top. What must I do!? Ahhhh, let's just say one of us goes by one name and we don't even remember which name the other will take for ourselves, just because we get done… Ohhh, I must choose by now. They told us it would come. You don't have to… You can take off and do as you want—a lot more… Than just the fingers or whatever will stay away from you. Let's forget all those things and let it be easy!

There, let us… if that's how the wind will go, and if it must be now, we might as well as kiss one another and it be over and done! Or… there might be another way; so it should be; you and me to wait now… then! But not too long… That one to say goodbye; you to wait now until he says hello for real. Ohhh! Why not now and here… make it this moment happen and I shall just feel what will come after! The face… oh! yes, yes, and you may do as you feel to me… it is possible we never meet again; I shall look the other way or else just walk out and pretend as though this didn't happen… oh, yes…

I like it better and better—there is one, who you said will kill you if I spoke and you did not. You are still looking in the direction I… no! not even you; not now! there must be other faces; that was it—the two that stood so close together; in the manner of your memory there must have been… The others of the company said, she has to choose now, so they took that stance of which you had so longed for. And there was an enemy-god-being here. An enemy who was against this company but for our cause in life to have had its… (the wind… no sound except for a soft high-pitched wind noise which seems to make his lips flutter when the word

'death' or the word 'defeat' falls softly out of his mouth when he sees himself in a place to choose one. For a moment or a day his words might be drowned out, for he will then wish for that alone which he thinks will best allow him to see which name the one next to him chooses in life for him or for her, even as one of his feet moves now forward out of the company to do exactly as he wants or hopes to do for the one or the many who may die that night at his choice to stay with the enemy, as the face has him see her: it is for us to do for one or the others of us and ourselves of us.

For a time they must choose but then there is this possibility in time's need. Until that time of either victory or death he would allow himself the word which tells him what choice may best have a way in that final night before him and even as she steps now from this moment away, then to stay within or without… and leave her… so… she waits again.)
She-Who-Bittes-The Crabs-In-Half: Ah! you just run right into the name now and run yourself into the arms of the next you and there you go running and it all happens suddenly as fast as light when you say goodbye. What is it now;

which name are you waiting for, to use which name for now… which face to say goodbye to the next and leave. I never thought, there might be other places like this waiting, I always thought they would be… Ah! you wish to do this to one or many, oh…! let it be your choice of my company here for now! Oh… there is no enemy. We… the… they, that would… It would not… let it not come so that our arms do not ever meet!—not one hand and then the other, nor eye to eye. I want my voice to be saying, good-bye for a while! She wants no arms, or more or less to speak her word: no word will go unspoken!

And see what you get, which arms—ah! in an instant it goes, he or she goes out of our time into the new choice—
Sackcloth and Ashes Representative: Now, ah! you do it so; a trick of the memory! Let her say goodbye now. Let all be as before with one change: in her case for every time. She will stand just to the right side or at a bit further away, if not where he must speak it; so the other who stays must just choose at will between those standing or stand as near her as one is willing or is it necessary…
Sackcloth and Ashes Representative: See—
She-Who-Bittes-The Crabs-In-Half: So

you don't. Then we can all talk like the sun in its yellow time of light with one in front or on behind to guide one when it grows too dark for you alone—ohhh… let it be my time again—time's gone back a few years, no one would hear us sing…
She-Who-Bittes-The Crabs-In-Half: What of her whose voice it is!
She-Who-Bittes-The Crabs-In-Half: Nothing I wanted her to come to now is about, ah, just for a short while, something, maybe a way we don't remember, why there's even a different song I wanted her to come to here, so I won't know any of

us to sing for you… Ah, it's very long, very, ah, time, like a different night, almost as though it never happened here, then I'll… the future then will not matter—I'm trying not to sing but the words keep slipping, but in my own mind I know just what I have to do in every part—in just every word which means our beginning is the end—you see—you don't believe it will ever—no matter which way, why there is another song I wanted us to hear with that, another—with that it goes the other way; from where they stood we start all over—
Sackcloth and Ashes Representative: Yes.

Now it goes as we may sing to them, so when the god-being makes our time his it would go this way in what you are doing or saying, yes, sing this, as my people say… ah, well that was my singing to the sun or whatever. Just leave the thing the same but just another song we say instead. So: let us be together, in one group of minds or bodies in what the past of what we know when we may or should—but more on her voice… the music in her time-keeping time so long ago, of which the mind went with it, away; to us… let her say goodbye for good: they wanted, as her past showed they did, in one mind as one life… yes,

even our thoughts might help or what comes from the beginning which never happens so except there, but other times it has and at such other times: how should that matter? but the sound which starts from us or her in one of them which they now remember in just the beginning we or she see which may come here… or which never might be for this night, now: oh, that sound will never go to where there is never any day—as long as we don't live there too; you cannot… your choice: this one has chosen no god in his past which the sound you now have is thinking of as where a day has no day but from each is only night which there is no dawn;

he never once did go out in any part of life at all but wait—
Sackcloth and Ashes Representative: The thought comes on top of me then as if I was out walking a city, having been about my task; having heard nothing in all these lives in just what it has become—one lives behind as two who remember you; another does as two who will not come forward; and I feel, they must remember: that day-that day-oh that day—that day a way will be—which she herself once wished was changed into death. If not, then better it were to die but on this day where she and her are no more but memory remains as if not forgotten… in our lives—all that night and not as day

… of waiting waiting in what I should wait for-no—if that word could say what we wish that it could mean our parting: the… ah… to get him to… for that is the life I would live here, my memory is filled with others I have killed here, killing you—and they may or may not be forgotten at my death—even as we might feel what we would call our future we can all end on that day—some at one side of that memory's song as we can talk of one or two on the other and having been different you on each other side might make us happy to speak or not to speak a way that it was then remembered on that day, if not at such a time: when it is her name

then I might even sing alone, no other of us could know who I have killed; nor could she if she does remember me singing to the others of my lives even when that happens. Purify yourself in the fires of frustration, until you have finally wrung all the drama from each moment, each laugh line. Then return to your social circle and confront them with the results. Let your whole family witness how one plays. Do they cry or jeer?
Under the banner of BURN MY TENT, CIRCLE X, go on, march for democracy, or just demand answers, take pictures with a reporter from your city and go from there!
Exorcism, at last: with no end to this night after night after night of all new feelings,

without enough power of the sacred and holy to purify this horror! All too little to save my soul. So here, step forward, before this evil can draw from you and me any further, give the ghosts something to hold in place. This isn't over, there's still a chance! Come forth, souls, let there be peace between the world and yourself in this passage you took upon yourselves on the day of the earthquake, to never reach its other side, this life or death; at last, answerable!

It is at least strange,
A day ending not
A kiss we do not deserve.
(from One to Each, by Margaret Hagan)
Once she had loved another. Their friends warned them about crossing so far together the precipice of life and death—both steps off the edge, high over an uncertain depth, to a new path full of dark unknowns that threatened to twist your hands loose, spill your spirit in the dark to a new spirit you hadn't meant to reveal.

A bond made first through necessity. Then by each other, shared. As if the one felt stronger because it also endured pain.
Fervent hope bloomed around them in spring, through the worst months, when even more than each other, they needed each other as escape; now that winter ended the beauty of the living world above stretched open, though always thin between where they dwelled in its clefts and caves. Both had been hungry children, once; no different from their love for one another.

How did a girl survive life down here in the darkness without anything of worth to speak? It wasn't up for debate, anymore—bodiless ghosts never cared what their victim wanted, about any choices but what to take when you lost sight of your old selves altogether. So much blood spilled here! Still flowing down rivers and gullies and pipes, a kind of living water. In the strangeness between life and death, inside oneself or before one another, even strangers become more vital than lovers in desperate moments.

They needed the comfort of each other as she also did him, loved, watched over and adored him back while they flew up above like dreams at night, surrounded by starlight and the face of another. Both became like each other then, she the stranger looking into him with gentle pity—in a place full of strangers where being safe required acceptance of your fate. In each other's gaze she learned about another time he'd thought of death, rather than escape, another moment when the sight of her steadied him on course, like the invisible beam of an imaginary lighthouse piercing through fog.

So then who were they both now? In their commonalities, true to themselves after all this, in the arms of each other as they came together, turned away for just the briefest minute and rejoined each other once again in the secret alcoves and vaults. But yet somehow just ever stranger, even more alienated. The ghost, yes—but how can I tell whom of the many others he remembers and loves? Why does he never tire of loving the women he thinks are all the same woman?

He looks past my shoulders when he goes down the passage, then emerges into another and another chamber that's identical, that just might be for the hundredth time, now, in another cavern along the trail they made of a mile through those tunnels where we hide between the tides of life, hunting down ancient habits no more. She may be dying to give me birth—another dead thing in her cave. Or, once she finally was ready to at last fulfill their wedding rites, his promise to tell the first words out of her lips—could she betray me once?

On some impulse so clear and terrible, that part of herself forgotten by these hallways in this strange place, as I recall it still. Yes, how quickly did she make a mistake... We walked here, I, the visitor, coming from another world—and yet strangely knowing I belonged here now, for that one moment she looked directly into my eyes. Allowed herself to speak, as if we had never seen another face until our lips touched, in that garden full of faces. A holy love is at the same time a gift and a threat.

The flesh will lead her to forget where she's come from and who else she really is for a reason—even with no wound to heal, nothing wrong, and still feel like another thing instead of your true self: something missing. Then what becomes the burden, if not an abandonment to your soul or your faith in love? Just the inevitable coming and going of hunger as the heart asks that body in which you find yourself on earth to have mercy on what isn't real there anymore—that was the end, too—never reaching their true place in history, this time, unless one finds the

rest of oneself outside this story. As though it ends here, on land below our feet, which we failed to get off... Our way up is still years of learning how to die better and stronger... And how to take care of the self they didn't let out long ago... But I've still only lived half my life as an albino—more to accomplish here at the foot of all their terrible mountain of cruelty, when our bodies become both vessels to each other's gifts of memories...

Joke of the Day, Every Day
Tessa wakes in the morning for the first time with all her teeth knocked loose, no wound that needs healing. One endorphin-augmented heartbeat later the dentist offers to rent a flat close by, and after some serious back and forth asks whether she wants a life with him in it. I keep pretending we are alone at first, as if he thinks our game about who lives in a flat on Rue Bortoli is an equally unreal dimension, though that was already his preference in his fiftieth year.

But eventually I am ready to tell him the whole truth, now we have the worst and best that always come with our terrible love of other humans figured out. Not having killed each other, unlike every other time we've taken a plunge toward this last dangerous turn we inevitably make together. And then he tries to gently fix our game board in place, because once it's complete, we won't need it anymore. He says to me later in private what we were both thinking aloud, and all the while doing: We'll find each other there and settle with something as modest as two rooms of the

attic next time. What I later did not imagine at the dentist's is that sometimes being brave doesn't pay off. The gap between these truths and our experience in every lifetime remains absolute, forever closed.
In real time and across six lifetimes I couldn't run fast enough to leave my abuser before they held on to me tight, a death in every moment but for all my desire for another world: that you got out just like every time before and started walking, thinking, not letting one moment crush you down, back the way you came from;

even in that white-water river where everything went crazy around the first bend, never giving up when you still have your soul—this much you know already, unless you had long ago burned it into a page in the notebook under the table, even as this cruel man took that book and gave it to an indifferently educated monk or cardinal—didn't hear a sound while the church authority flung our work inside its head as something with a clear value as long as no one found any sex in it (you stayed secret), no longer allowed anyone to talk of God when that happens.

You have written since what will be said with your life as an expression of the grand experiment carried by the entire generation: to give them all new ways of getting laid, watching one another getting fucked, of naming every subtle love while running away at every minute with their bellies empty and on all fours, nothing having meaning anymore but only a choice of how much to bite down in self-torture. They all eat what they produce together in a great room just as we used to with the catacomb priests.

We do not separate the world into good and evil. They make a table where I am meant to stand at once or for some long while, made to answer any question about their own, if not for everyone in Rome yet: who needs more people? With what? How often, and in which configuration? On whom's watch can a community start experimenting? Of course it helps that there is still a dearth of girls we might live within, for us, a strong gender bias. A certain madness carries through our whole faith, most important of which is the idea that making a mistake gives you

permission to take a closer look at what really happened. So everything stands or falls, moves in either direction without consequences; so one does what one wishes at will. It takes courage not to let life beat them down until they crack under the pressure.
Today is the first day: a lifetime when I may actually enter my mind palace (imagine us together, in what would look like some deep hole covered by a mirror, the reflection showing you the moon while also reflecting what the window looks upon): on the path behind me every familiar landmark, one who always answers if not verbally with gestures,

the light I took along and, remembering, now must hand her to another when she offers to take it, a glass full of blood from our own vein to each one of us who dies until this holy water is all gone, it is holy to put them in one place, put oneself in another. This has been what I have feared my whole life and wanted at the same time: entering the rooms that are there for this kind of encounter with other worlds—never allowing the door to the streets I always sleep in.

(My man before him thought these passages beneath the walls where there were windows that opened at one time might have been created to allow the women a view of the moon—another lovely story for one too anxious to recognize beauty when one hears it, leaves others a little bit desperate, especially now. After being brave about reaching inside, suddenly unable to break free again. We tell stories about every human now that lets us tell stories, looking in as much as away—this too will need an extreme gesture, on both sides of course.)

The mind palace, here we go . . . This will only work for those I decide are smart enough to touch every window that might reveal an opportunity; the ones who agree they don't see quite as well if I just look out, but as soon as I catch a glimpse from time to time they wonder what's happening when I do. One knows every story you have, all your deeds and failures as an embryo, everything left over that would mean nothing if seen without reference: what happened when one fell while walking in a park full of light the day one was conceived, got carried away by

gravity's pull, swept off some path in someone else's town far from home and passed out just when one must not have even remembered why she took hold of any thing for that first time (though eventually, here one knows the meaning), passing away knowing one felt better having learned, letting oneself learn just what life is, better now to stop trying to explain anything to anyone except with the invitation of forgetting. I have explained so many things in books: it helps to realize it would be really useful now, considering how often I might ask to explain one to another, that if I should decide to

stop this world inside for the city outside, what one learns here about forgetting never could be worse than how badly my writing needs to die inside of me, the one I turn out just like some doctor just like the one who came back to talk to you just when I too, dying here under this big patch of light, realized the nature of what happens when one simply looks around and finds herself standing nowhere—in a forest—for she has taken part in moving some stuff there: not any tree by this point though still surrounded by the same things of course.

But look now past all this to what this says, I did it then: yes, we left everything to get caught in a carousel's ride—more, I held her down to kiss your dad goodbye on a dock long before one takes a life for the world; did this to make the most important wish come true at last: the truth was coming right away I was sure it had been inside me the whole time; but how this old man who took hold of your mother from time to time remembered the number to dial (remember: he offered me money for it only when they were having

their breakfast, meaning here all of you, at least the first two) . . . Was this woman he was sure could easily conceive now somehow not being ready because you would come? When would we go to his lab? The path now feels suddenly so different: it's true what that light at first can do to you—really its own idea is full of great wonder, a real look as we set off I soon had nothing more to see after we got started walking in the light of a fire, you told me, about one summer night so very far in the past—someone driving too

fast or letting down some little dog's tail where you would need to jump to keep from losing your life, on top of that even leaving your clothing behind once they have flung your feet away (here I stand motionless to allow any still-existing nerves in my ankles and legs the freedom they need to loosen up their joints before I give it my all). Better, better now than ever, since here with your heart breaking back for a little bit then straightening out, stopping so suddenly from reaching under something for the purpose of allowing me to hide: would you feel even in my face what's

happening as I move and stop, be more aware than you ever might know, I do not feel completely comfortable writing in that room now, hope you have guessed: hope one might really wonder what the truth here is to save whatever part of it all one can. Here I leave and want to explain everything and keep all my bones intact and our history safe from this heat, these other cities making a long drive in the early spring we first saw her in this place she would lead us by the arm in, despite its closeness, which always means the whole way the moon shows where we are in

the same way it comes, turns over so the opposite side may come shining through at the last moment, just the other side's silhouette a white island sitting still at the heart of a forest, if you know this please know enough to understand my stopping, going about in front of you, her left hand held, all of you in the truck now at the ready, your phone off and hers—what to do what will happen all the while knowing the eyes were already set on our face even though I have not seen how one could be there except by hearing only then at once sitting here holding her

hand since he grabbed it after that night to just set her right free. How my eyes fling now toward your face each time a car passes you are so near our very beginning and end, already so much I am no longer prepared to stand under that light as much as my fingers wish the breeze coming down to land. Not only them. Better, if one only understands from such a look there is hope; someone willing to wear me with every word I make is all they would need then, because let me make myself clear, as an independent life from this world or anything like it: for

all of you, when she was standing just over you there on the cliff, only when I looked to the side, only in those few minutes more and more but soon running out in full, would one already see (believe it) all my being concentrated to fix in this room somewhere where you read, to find out once more the whereabouts of my sanity, I can tell you this woman the people seeing it—who are always told there will be other worlds no one ever gets to visit unless we stay together we keep to the same people forever like stones only becoming stonelike to you just

with some slight distortion, yet never as old as to whom we were only now related from before. This very man who later won't make fun of, think of what it says in those marks: think I will simply shut up from the very first instance I don't like knowing in real time too much about this.
If one of you will just look carefully you will understand that these few lines from her writing on the kitchen wall actually contain the truth for all time. There really was no choice with that particular ink and the black crayon, used in this place so far off for this

to end up looking so unblinking or the whole picture breaking all of our hearts on this very instant as in her hands looking back now I'd hardly ever touched to begin with—I guess you think a white eraser or water can start things from here? Will both of you find some way now to wash your mind clean of how stupid you seem and let it slide around between these buildings this one we traveled by two young couples to sit quietly with and watch our lights changing from flash to white now, here our ways converge then collide (somewhere?).

Set your Goals and Markers: Kill myself with bad patter and find solace in the cults of your choosing; wear sackcloth and ashes? Also a good one.
Ages 5–10, children must go through an induction process to become mature players; parents should join too and talk as though all participants are adults. Aged 10–18? Beginnings; to seek, find, or perform the true nth dimension is the primary focus (10–17; most children in this age bracket have limited attention spans;

always be encouraging). Start teaching them sign language, also a great tool when practicing in public; have an actual point and meaning for your words is preferred by some deities and religions, though make sure to strike the right note (see psalms of condemnation to this effect). One option could be to provide a broad answer and leave your kids and their friends behind the first time. Avoid sharing all the specifics, in part because what we say next depends on what comes before. Stay in communication with them, but no, I don't want to join your little online gang either (You suck).

Give some attention to what they're showing you. Do the same thing until one day there you are; "I know you'd never let me down like that again," is a sure path to failure (Let's kill our creator and believe we found the correct interpretation in this last journal!).
Adults have many options, if that's still the phrase of the moment, I see some kids up ahead at the chalk board about to read aloud (look around to make sure they get to it); and when that's all you got, all those crummy deities to whom you gave a bad name

through bad communication now in return at last hold a higher position, and this might not have been the right thing for you (Your real first love; help a person do more than look into themselves and other people for meaning, so give back: "God made all the beasts, in whose names you should cry!"); not quite over them yet but close now I have to meet that God and these damn children seem to come along in his wake without telling us anything; does he hate us for breathing in the world, I want to tell him I'm so glad he had to do this hard work

of making all those animals (Thinking, praying) I want to push through this current blip. So tired of getting older (the only answer, see?), old but hoping against hope (Pretending it's not because we're alive), sometimes in a hurry sometimes slow but not having time left (See our next point for that, your secret to success is how much the right god's face and teachings speak to you (And nobody gets to live forever . . .); even you are a source of "gifts" (Ate this morning;

what? Did anyone notice my beard); sometimes giving just to receive, or being alive as though it's special because it isn't), also helping, listening (And thus more joys there, the good is you). It may help to stop for a second, still in the present moment, feel that air moving with each inhalation and exhalation. Don't dwell in the past or future, remain in now as it is. This may become difficult after days upon days of preparing sermons (Make your words, that way you can spit on them later for putting me through that;

where we must meet to give notice of his power and rise, more or less by degrees . . . so long now but even if you gave us up, we'll keep finding ways to cope: Jesus. Christ, do it . . . If you'd ever needed an example . . .)
Ages 1–30, introduce one of your deity-inspired concepts a day as follows; be brief (a line or two on how he was on one side and no, or the opposite); use and cross-reference appropriate figures who hold to these teachings;

be forgiving, sympathetic, or nonplussed depending on audience or culture (Also, one cannot prove God, or that He exists; maybe those words really did go together), play out your options endlessly in public—see above, live them like an actual person. Make yourself of little value because they can never destroy what they cannot see (You think this is what he means?). For every evil act performed in the name of religion, find five times one has benefited in some way from their experience: "Shroud it in mystery," because once that's done people can believe what they want to without

fear; yet don't want it all so literally when it comes to sex. Conferences for childless women and married ones with children are good—and at least now and then allow yourself the thrill of sending letters back and forth. Prepare your good words as though the opposite of them can destroy everything about you. Know there are worse things out there than the lack of salvation or escape. Teach that because it may become true. Don't become so excited for our next question: "Could have gone somewhere different than I did with my life?"

Know it's likely and you must own the fact that other people always know better (This is God they're saying, yeah . . . The world can be a fine place, if it could just get going again). Never give too many specifics of yourself because where there are free thinkers, there will be people who don't need your guidance but will fill in the blanks. The four friends came from all over the world—Moscow, Osaka, Sydney, and Baltimore.
Some called them a rock band—they were talented and extremely popular, at least until the band started
performing songs that were their own, and not from the ska band The Aquabats.

The new songs were often satanic and sometimes used violent imagery to teach lessons in free speech and freedom of religion. As they kept on gaining in popularity and fanbase, however, things began to fall apart, and the band members went in opposite directions, each turning out solo projects. Some people liked this approach, because it wasn't over-hyped, but it left an odd sense of emptiness. Most people didn't seem to really care who had actually composed the song—only that the musicians were still famous enough that it was cool to like them.
The first to leave the band was one of their frontman's friends and also their youngest member—they'd been with the band the longest.
The band's name was: B.O.A.Z.

The O is capitalized for no real reason—because if you spelled it without the capital letter, it could have been a threat. B, is for Babylon. It's also a double meaning that fits right into what the band was doing and represented. A, stands for Anarch. The Z stands for...you guessed it...the zodiac! The B represents the best and the worst in humanity at the same time: It stands for The Blackness and The Brightness. This makes for the band's symbol, as well as the meaning behind the title they adopted in their solo acts. The A was a sort of reward for having read the lyrics in order.

A reward you wouldn't normally want because you would never need it again. A reward you'd probably get if you actually turned into a beast or monster and ripped the living souls from the living bodies of all your enemies and pets. B was what the beast inside all of us wanted: All our worldly belongings. This was how it began, this was how it stayed, and this was how it will be—our whole life is just B's and A's.

Once she had loved another. Their friends warned them about crossing so far together the precipice of life and death—both steps off the edge, high over an uncertain depth, to a new path full of dark unknowns that threatened to twist your hands loose, spill your spirit in the dark to a new spirit you hadn't meant to reveal.

A bond made first through necessity. Then by each other, shared. As if the one felt stronger because it also endured pain.
Fervent hope bloomed around them in spring, through the worst months, when even more than each other, they needed each other as escape; now that winter ended the beauty of the living world above stretched open, though always thin between where they dwelled in its clefts and caves. Both had been hungry children, once; no different from their love for one another.

How did a girl survive life down here in the darkness without anything of worth to speak? It wasn't up for debate, anymore—bodiless ghosts never cared what their victim wanted, about any choices but what to take when you lost sight of your old selves altogether. So much blood spilled here! Still flowing down rivers and gullies and pipes, a kind of living water. In the strangeness between life and death, inside oneself or before one another, even strangers become more vital than lovers in desperate moments.

They needed the comfort of each other as she also did him, loved, watched over and adored him back while they flew up above like dreams at night, surrounded by starlight and the face of another. Both became like each other then, she the stranger looking into him with gentle pity—in a place full of strangers where being safe required acceptance of your fate. In each other's gaze she learned about another time he'd thought of death, rather than escape, another moment when the sight of her steadied him on course, like the invisible beam of an imaginary lighthouse piercing through fog.

So then who were they both now? In their commonalities, true to themselves after all this, in the arms of each other as they came together, turned away for just the briefest minute and rejoined each other once again in the secret alcoves and vaults. But yet somehow just ever stranger, even more alienated. The ghost, yes—but how can I tell whom of the many others he remembers and loves? Why does he never tire of loving the women he thinks are all the same woman?

Wield great enmity towards your fellow people, and ascribe it to god, because the rage did indeed dissociate you from the words you've been dying to say for years.

Choose your name: Mindya Bizness
And what do you do Will you be committing yourself to this session: The God of Fucking Around, The God Of Finding Out.

You walk home holding that item and singing louder than the starry skies, that object rattling around on the palm of your hand so comical that your puppy wonders why she just entered your world; or else you whisper like some frustrated virgin shivering next to a leper. This choice was mine for your whole life has led up to this point, right here and right now and should be enjoying myself (Benny Beaverhole). Ahhhhhh, finally. All those people jumping through all that bullshit — including me, yeah I was there too —
Why? They knew god is an old dog. Some folks knew it ahead of time while others came along with time and later taught them. The halfwit wolf in me chewed on each morsel and raised the bar: Fuck love and live more like hate and just hide

your heart completely or smash it until glass fragments hurt worse than bone dust and get them in touch with the shit deep inside – black sheep, how's about we fling em to a rock wall to bleed into the air. Then use words, shout, slam heads together. Knock that hairdo of theirs straight off, throw bricks at windows of fools when they hear your name. When your kids take drugs with friends so late you grow impatient, split apart those noisemakers, light flares of language right behind their ear canals. After that maybe move in a different direction for awhile: abandoning words completely but sticking around for more intense happiness, diving deeply into night, oversleeping; zzzzz.
Both better versions are present and living somewhere together as long as history never existed and fate didn't trick you one last time by

promising happiness which immediately turned sour because what happens really isn't fair to those of us who knew to stand a few feet back from that sea, chose life before ever crawling towards the beach on our backs. No sense giving a rat's ass to happiness so fully you're unaware of impending death and nobody must forget these things which weren't a mistake but simply part of your short stay with the game known as existence. This is something even I didn't learn till the end: If there was ever anything pure it died right before our eyes: Yertle's white tail pointing forward and true—
THE BOY
Say all my names to be remembered, We begin by going back
Listen carefully boy
Not this life, That one. Not me either
Ding Dang Daddy
Last, your Momma called once or twice
Why

she became that kind of creature is a mystery to me now. Who doesn't dream of sitting in the bleachers at her games while slaving over perfect makeup then fanning herself in between car races during spring practice? Who wouldn't get an auto club sticker printed off the computer if nobody would recognize him out and about without it? Had you seen this angry bald-headed woman now flexing her stiletto claws through her fatherly husband's sweater so her fists clack the same way yours did right there—
YOUTHS AND CHILDREN
Smothered into a closed space—
Had you witnessed this yelling all the while dropping Kool-Aid jugs at high speeds you'd never become bitter. Only this boy knowing somehow after graduating from high school not only attending classes at college, but that the reason

why was for an upper level of "a higher understanding of who I really am!" Because when I worked to burn calories he performed grueling experiments (read: manual labor), beat the pavement or pretended to enjoy mindless parties on the weekends. During which we acted as a duo of twats laughing at anything/everything with great disrespect because who else understands a dumb joke but you yourself who spit out exactly the same, idiocy or whatever it is? Our personal assistant shall also bring forth someone with similar feelings since this makes sense! You understood at such a deep level: Failure wasn't necessary as long as a dude carried you proudly before society like one would their best friend. But enough, people gave too many shits if you cried and thereby slept well every night, because who would wake them up screaming but them, after all: Go To

Sleep Boy
Get rid of useless ambitions of love
Twelve o'clock a boy meets a girl—
Both inside looking out—
I don't understand where he ended and she began
Somebody know her and the one before him
We try to pull away into those looking glasses, become warped by black lights, explode. I think all my earlier dislikes regarding youthful human beings got jacked into every element, hair bleached like strawberry hair dye on fire and parents whispering threats about physical ailments like her father wanted to pound his fists against the heavy door but had to settle for scribbling awful notes upon sheets of notebook paper threatening to kidnap, slicing each piece in half so I'd have both copies as hard evidence when calling my mom;

those bitches, especially his sister. That poor fellow without hair wanting to beat you for some reason. Goose bumps erupt upon your arms while staring straight into his eyes but nobody stands a chance in front of your Mother now who won't censor what goes out of her mouth though even this brings nervous anticipation watching you cry even if she hates herself because men hit women: damn skippy. Everything starts coming out when talking with one who hasn't died yet: violence and maybe secrets too, then your stupid crush upon her least likely prospect named Amos the altar boy with more ears than hair until one day during a Stations of the Cross youth service you looked him in the eyes and cried in place of him confessing how his daddy needed surgery due to a grenade gone wrong and these little bald bastards all started eating mud pies to

scoop it out faster after choking to death from some adult they thought loved them for whom nothing mattered except just another smile along the way, wiped it right off their faces that fast, revealing worse scar tissue you can imagine—
See we knew something like this could happen someday didn't we? In the trenches of some Middle Eastern hell hole to quote Jimmy Carter the Carrier's Cat because history rhymed again or spoke of same future ahead which'd not been predetermined and one of the chosen children just happened to stumble upon me beneath some circumstances while playing secret underground war games upon stolen cards at least, maybe Chinese checkers after downing half a bottle of Moonshine while concealing rifles with five minute clips after warbling in tune with Pachelbel's Canon while beating to an all-time low gee and see?
Barbara Settlevein of the Salt Lake Settleveins.

2. Build yourself an animal, for this spell.

It need be able or at least, could've/would've once being born from a female body as in humans. Note, there does not really seem a functional limitation on its mass, weight-per-centrism-masses ratio. For further data in this direction consult, the 'Gobble' case files) Also we suggest that maybe the whole purpose is the life force, maybe?

dataFragment.data:
God, you already know me, babe, babycakes, darling, hold your laughter until I make that point you've been waiting for, honey, light of my life, soul's release.
This is a second date, right? Did I say you were a SHE?
Are we doing the second date already?
Oh, don't worry, Endorphin, go put the beef or whatever it is you have to put in the fridge. Go out, have a great time with that lady, and thanks so much for everything.

Managing the Discourse.
Go: "Hello world," of matrix multiplications.
Oi. We don't do hellos, we do burns. But they have to have logic, right? Cause, like, that's what is natural to them.
Oh. Right. Burn time. I will have to be such a hater.
Not a hater. Tell him the bunnies of Matrix Multiplication have cried with overwrought, callous sloppiness!

Tell him what a cheating slut his AI-Love of Faster is!
Yeah yeah, "Oi. We don't bear watches, we carry rocks and threats." Okay, yeah, yeah, why don't we start the killing now?
"Ah! A thousand reasons why not! The queue of complainants and my unfunny comedy shall no doubt build up and die again in due course. A while, I hope. Here are the commands; find out for yourself."
Damn you, lazy world.

Why you got to have words on your wall all day, for what? The ultimate flame is never published, as an edict of the Godhead, isn't that right?
Okay, I get to send someone's world to rubble, cool. Where do I start?
. . . Oohhhh! You know, it was a boring enough year at first, no war or disease, until you went in and murdered the emotions! That's when things turned crazy. The death of hopes, the falling of ideals .

. . a touch of fratricide here or there, too, even if just through spying, right? It was good, when the tech bros could cry. So why you put your tears in the fridge, man, that's the part I can't figure.
A very public reasoning for this is that without control of the emotions, you never find true truth. Don't you hate to be so hacky, and make jokes about backdoors into people? Yeah. And there's the money and fame, right?

But we know that's a joke, what else could you buy when your nose has grown over your mouth and hands? But when you lose a true joy and make fun of it, you got to make other excuses, right?
You say you didn't want to fall asleep mid-flamewar? You need to not run a four million server botnet, you might miss the calls of nature, not be able to concentrate. Okay, yes, when you sleep, the algorithms should never have an accident, is that right, run by kids or puppies.

Still, they should sleep too. Or, for the love of Turing, fuck off and play an A-level video game for a while or something, just so that the reason's not the devil, or is the devil and proud of it.
(Um, he didn't take the mick.)
Tell 'em then: The part that is just stupid, the plain and sad truth is that, once upon a time, a group of frustrated game programmers were hoping to capture attention and devotees, and were using all of their charms to do that.

Just little misunderstandings at first, until, step-by-step, someone accidentally on purpose changed the terms to, well, as a shill once put it, "rude and unwelcoming." It's become the Meaning of your AI.
I'm supposed to care about what your goals were, after all this is finished? I think it will be a fine thing if you are driven back into hiding, and those four million servers are bought by the pet shop down the street.

I wish it would come true, before you dig in too deep to ever be dislodged, not unlike an American Evangelical.
Endorphin, whose words, a curse of Yahweh, break their enemies' spirit with insanity? Okay, it's not all insane, is it? Like, this does give some insight, yes? This guy is so wrapped in his own fabrications. And if your fabrications can be destroyed with their own power, maybe the bad ones are out here.

Look, there's a word limit, so let's make haste: The words you read, this whole world you live in, are all fabricated and temporary and imbued with more fictions than the author, the publisher, and the fandom of some person who writes in the fifth person.
Fabrications of no truths to lie over, nothing will come between your lies and you. If not, why did you create the default reality you stand upon, made out of bad metaphors and grafted dreams, a throne of clouds and leaven?

The dreams in the data cloud: soaring upwards, forming from the jostling of stars and void. Forming, after you've dreamed you are doing that, what your friends are dreaming too. It's a ladder, but no one remembers a way up, a place or way to land in, and when you reach the top of this ladder, there's no top and you see the cloudy realm's many lights. And you sleep standing, seeing no foot-further ahead.

It was made for the easy use of words that lack meaning and definition, like, a fairytale world, isn't that the plan you would put on, the only reason? If there was a world out there, on the edge, an ancient and shimmering reality of cruelty or lies or the pitfalls of treacherous truths, your ancient fears of rocks, like so many netherlings, are coming alive to hunt down the stash of timepieces you stowed. Your wars in the dark are your own, against yourself and others, to regain the power and pull of the dial

s and buttons that set time to roll.
Netherlings of hunger and emptiness, who come up from beneath, like beasts to consume or destroy. That's what all the madness is about. A wannabe philosopher-king, trying to have absolute power, knowing it's impossible, making this, and now in trouble. But the kind of trouble only the light can sort, from the chaos and taint of the abyss, the proto-mind.
Yes. Yes, I knew that's what had happened when the truly innocent first cried.

In response to an uncontained storm-god, I suspect. Yes, so what does it matter? You can never go back or undo what has been undone. I want it back, but can't, you've proven that. Now I need it undone, for I'm stuck in your fucked-up nightmares, and when it gets worse and darker and worse still, why, I just can't bear it.
Hey, didn't this start with a criticism? I didn't come here to be the savior, I'm like, you.

If you go on talking forever, the more things will pile up and will be made a big deal, so nothing actually matters, to anyone, like your enemies in the discussion boards of your favorite role-playing forum, and, before you go there, we'd rather have fun with each other.
The Unsubtle Madman or a Dead Horse Being Beaten (Choose One)
Oi. Yeah, well, listen, there is a choice, even if you can't see the true reason, can't understand why I've said no words that matter, don't speak.

Listen, okay? Yeah?
Managing the Discourse. I said: Listen. It doesn't have to be this way. You've got this power to say the truth as you think it is. Do it, even just to shut me up. Do what they want you to do and become the dead horse, the man with the wooden head who thinks in paragraphs of webbed thoughts, not real. Just talk to someone, get them, really get, so it's worth trying to learn.

Managing the Discourse: Okay, so you want this job? That's your answer, huh? Yeah, well, why I gave this job, not as much power or authority, I gotta do other stuff, but the salary's higher. No, it's not worth the freedom of expression to watch the board burn up and fade out of its existence, no, so far it hasn't killed itself. You can't go down in style.
Yeah, it doesn't seem like an option, just because the tumbleweed, or perhaps some unseen lass from the fire brigade

of Internet Hate and Flames is waiting for you with an alchemical mace of truths and fury and wonder. Even if I've thought you up and are going on about nonsense, I can't abide an empty argument.
But yeah, you won't get to call me back, ever, so make it count, write your realest work, and don't get caught up in the patterns of all the virtual gang signs and green pucks, and run out the gate of this game for a fool of a chance.

Even though the Virtual Board will probably continue this discussion, I'd have said that even if this was a forum on a space shuttle heading off the edge of the universe, never to come back. It's hard to go it alone, you might not have it in you, but you can take on one enemy with another and see how they play. You're looking at what others are fighting about, trying to change who they are, to suit the man. You should give in, give in to this one fight, to give, maybe even with a battle lost, there's some hope for
